subject: Verbal Reasoning
title: EduTest-style Year 5 Verbal Reasoning — Practice Paper 1

questions.prompt: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to ___
questions.explanation: A puppy is a young dog, so a kitten is a young cat.

questions.prompt: Finger is to hand as toe is to ___
questions.explanation: Fingers are part of a hand, so toes are part of a foot.

questions.prompt: Hot is to cold as generous is to ___
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites. The opposite of generous is mean.

questions.prompt: Library is to books as gallery is to ___
questions.explanation: A library is a place that holds books; a gallery is a place that holds paintings.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Rose, tulip, daisy and lily are all flowers. An oak is a tree.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Square, circle, triangle and rectangle are flat (2D) shapes. A cube is a solid (3D) shape.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Copper, iron, gold and silver are all metals. Plastic is not a metal.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: March, June, October and January are months. Monday is a day of the week.

questions.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "ancient"?
questions.explanation: "Ancient" means very old, so its opposite is "modern", meaning new or of the present time.

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "rapid"?
questions.explanation: "Rapid" means happening fast, which is closest to "quick".

questions.prompt: Which word means about the same as "brave"?
questions.explanation: "Brave" and "courageous" both describe someone who faces danger or difficulty without fear.

questions.prompt: "Reluctant" most nearly means ___
questions.explanation: Someone who is reluctant does not want to do something, so "reluctant" means "unwilling".

questions.prompt:
Which letter comes next in this series?
A, C, E, G, ___
questions.explanation: The series skips one letter each time (A, _, C, _, E, _, G, _). After G, skipping H, comes I.

questions.prompt: If CAT is written in code as DBU, how is DOG written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward in the alphabet: C→D, A→B, T→U. So D→E, O→P, G→H gives EPH.

questions.prompt:
Which letter comes next in this series?
Z, X, V, T, ___
questions.explanation: The series goes backwards through the alphabet, skipping one letter each time: Z, (Y), X, (W), V, (U), T, (S), R.

questions.prompt: In a code, MONDAY is written as NPOEBZ. How is FRIDAY written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: M→N, O→P, N→O, D→E, A→B, Y→Z. Doing the same to FRIDAY gives G, S, J, E, B, Z.

questions.prompt: Maya is older than Leo but younger than Kim. Who is the oldest?

options.label: D
options.text: They are all the same age

questions.explanation: Maya is younger than Kim, and Leo is younger than Maya. So Kim is the oldest.

questions.prompt: In a race, Priya finished before Quinn. Quinn finished before Raj. Sara finished after Raj. Of these four runners, who finished last?
questions.explanation: The order is Priya, Quinn, Raj, then Sara after Raj. Sara finished last.

questions.prompt: All Zibs are Zabs. No Zabs are Zubs. Can a Zib be a Zub?

options.label: D
options.text: Only if it is also a Zab

questions.explanation: Every Zib is a Zab, and no Zab is a Zub. So no Zib can be a Zub.

questions.prompt: Three children stand in a line. Rob is shorter than Tom. Sam is shorter than Rob. Who is the tallest?

options.label: D
options.text: They are all the same height

questions.explanation: Sam is shorter than Rob, and Rob is shorter than Tom. So Tom is the tallest.
